rows.title: Categorical Fisher Positivity on Simplex Tangents

maturity_record.invariant: The inherited Fisher metric is strictly positive on every certified nonzero categorical simplex tangent under full support, while a duplicated-score model exhibits an explicit nonzero null direction.
maturity_record.assumption_review: CategoricalFisherCarrier packages a full-support law, an existing ScoreModel, and exact metric and lowering-map representations on simplex tangents. The general positivity theorem depends on this certificate. A separate genuine Fin 2 categorical construction proves that its one-dimensional simplex tangent space is spanned by (1,-1) and is positive definite there; no claim is made that every arbitrary score parameterization is full rank.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: The explicit Fin 2 categorical law and nonzero tangent (1,-1) have Fisher energy exactly four, and every Fin 2 simplex tangent is a multiple of that direction. Duplicated score coordinates separately give a nonzero tangent with zero Fisher energy.

rows.title: Fisher Pullback under Reparameterization

maturity_record.invariant: Pulling the existing finite Fisher metric through a composite Jacobian equals successive pullback, and every such pullback is positive semidefinite.
maturity_record.assumption_review: Outcome and coordinate carriers are finite and Jacobians are finite real matrices. No invertibility is needed for pullback or semidefiniteness, so a rank-deficient chart may retain null directions; positive definiteness is not claimed here.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Nonidentity rectangular Jacobians exercise genuine reparameterization, while a rank-deficient matrix demonstrates why the conclusion is nonnegative rather than strictly positive.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep101_fisherPullback_reparameterization and fep101_fisherPullback_nonnegative on the inherited ScoreModel Fisher carrier.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep101_fisherPullback_reparameterization:
theorem fep101_fisherPullback_reparameterization
    (model : ScoreModel Outcome d)
    (outer : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin k) ℝ)
    (inner : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin d) ℝ)
    (left right : Fin d → ℝ) :
    pullbackMetric model (outer * inner) left right =
      pullbackMetric model outer (inner.mulVec left) (inner.mulVec right)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep101_fisherPullback_nonnegative:
theorem fep101_fisherPullback_nonnegative
    (model : ScoreModel Outcome d)
    (jacobian : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin k) ℝ) (tangent : Fin k → ℝ) :
    0 ≤ pullbackMetric model jacobian tangent tangent

rows.statement_review: PullbackMetric for matrix composition is successive pullback and remains positive semidefinite. No invertibility is assumed; outer d-by-k and inner k-by-d map back to d, rather than the maximally general three-independent-dimension signature.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The matrices are supplied linear maps, called Jacobians by interpretation; no actual derivative of a coordinate chart is certified. Positive definiteness requires separate injectivity and score-identifiability support. The appropriate bilinear pullback is J-transpose*F*J; do not replace it by J*F*J-transpose.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Use a nonscalar rectangular outer and inner with compatible dimensions; evaluate the same inherited Fisher bilinear form after composition.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: A zero or rank-deficient Jacobian gives null pullback even if the original metric is positive definite. Actual nonlinear coordinate maps require a HasFDerivAt/chain-rule bridge.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 038 has an algebraic scalar candidate-Jacobian factorization with a previously identified missing coordinate derivative bridge.101 generalizes matrix pullback algebra but does not repair that missing derivative fact.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Fisher pullback composes under finite reparameterization and remains positive semidefinite.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds arbitrary finite Jacobian matrices between the existing ScoreModel Fisher carrier and new chart coordinates.

touching_relations.rationale: Finite-matrix Fisher pullback composition extends the original scalar Bernoulli pullback identity without asserting a global chart theorem. Reviewed 2026-09-22 against the primary-qualified endpoint rule. The witness carries fep-038 through its reviewed supporting theorem `fep_fep038.FEP038.fep038_fisherMetric_pullback` rather than the primary `fep_fep038.FEP038.fep038_fisherInformation_eq`; the row stands unchanged.

rows.title: Unbiased Scalar Cramér–Rao Bound under Score Regularity

maturity_record.invariant: Finite unbiased scalar estimation under score regularity and positive Fisher information satisfies variance times Fisher information at least one.
maturity_record.assumption_review: ScalarCramerRaoCertificate explicitly records centered unbiasedness, unit estimator–score covariance, and strictly positive scalar Fisher information for an existing one-parameter ScoreModel. The theorem does not derive score regularity by differentiating a parameterized family or cover biased estimators.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Positive Fisher information rules out an identically zero score, and unit score covariance rules out a constant centered estimator, so the Cauchy–Schwarz bound cannot be discharged by a degenerate zero product.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep102_unbiasedScalar_cramerRao with unbiasedness, score regularity, and Fisher positivity fields explicit.

theorem fep102_unbiasedScalar_cramerRao
    (model : ScoreModel Outcome 1) (estimator : Outcome → ℝ)
    (target : ℝ)
    (certificate : ScalarCramerRaoCertificate model estimator target) :
    1 ≤ estimatorVariance model.law estimator target * scalarFisher model

The certificate includes unbiasedness, scoreRegularity=1 and positive Fisher; the proof uses the latter two, while unbiasedness makes the squared centered error a variance interpretation.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: ScoreModel is centered score data. Parameterized-family differentiation, estimator independence of the parameter and interchange regularity are not derived. The stated product bound is well-defined finite real algebra; positive Fisher allows dividing to a reciprocal bound.

rows.title: Natural-Gradient Equivariance under an Invertible Full-Rank Chart

maturity_record.invariant: Under invertible Fisher and chart matrices, the natural gradient transports equivariantly so lowering the chart-coordinate vector yields the pulled-back covector.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The finite ScoreModel Fisher matrix and square chart Jacobian each carry an Invertible instance. Rank-deficient metrics or charts are excluded because the natural-gradient and chart-coordinate inverses would not be uniquely defined. The supporting weighted Cauchy–Schwarz theorem requires positive right energy.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Nonidentity invertible charts change vector coordinates while preserving the lowered covector law; the proof spike also excludes a zero-energy right vector before deriving its finite weighted inequality.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep103_naturalGradient_equivariance and fep103_weightedCauchySchwarz_proofSpike with both invertibility boundaries.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep103_naturalGradient_equivariance:
theorem fep103_naturalGradient_equivariance
    (model : ScoreModel Outcome d) [Invertible (fisherMatrix model)]
    (jacobian : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) [Invertible jacobian]
    (covector : Fin d → ℝ) :
    chartPullbackLower model jacobian
        (chartCoordinates jacobian (naturalGradient model covector)) =
      chartCovector jacobian covector
qualified_declaration_statements.fep103_weightedCauchySchwarz_proofSpike:
theorem fep103_weightedCauchySchwarz_proofSpike
    (law : FiniteLaw Outcome) (left right : Outcome → ℝ)
    (hRight : 0 < ∑ outcome, law outcome * right outcome ^ 2) :
    (∑ outcome, law outcome * left outcome * right outcome) ^ 2 ≤
      (∑ outcome, law outcome * left outcome ^ 2) *
        ∑ outcome, law outcome * right outcome ^ 2

rows.statement_review: With both ambient Fisher matrix and square chart matrix invertible, inverse-vector transport and transpose-covector transport satisfy pulled-back lowering. Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz is an independently supplied supporting proof.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The vector is J-inverse*v; covector J-transpose*c; lowering is J-transpose*F*J. These orientations are essential. An arbitrary supplied covector need not be an actual derivative of an objective. No Hessian transformation or nonlinear global-chart theorem follows; Hessian pullback would need objective/chart differentiability and generally second-derivative terms.

rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Singular Fisher/duplicated score or singular chart cannot meet the invertibility contracts. For a nonsymmetric invertible2D chart, omitting transpose changes covector transport.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 100 tangent full rank does not imply ambient inverse exists;038 scalar interior duality gives a valid full-rank example. Keep formalized for exact linear algebra.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Natural gradients transform equivariantly under an invertible full-rank finite chart.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds invertible Fisher and chart matrices plus explicit vector and covector coordinate transports.

rows.title: Mirror-Descent Three-Point Identity

maturity_record.invariant: The algebraic Bregman expression associated with supplied potential and gradient data obeys the exact three-point identity used by mirror descent.
maturity_record.assumption_review: The coordinate carrier is finite and potential and gradient are arbitrary supplied functions. The identity is algebraic and assumes neither convexity nor that the gradient is the derivative of the potential; those extra properties are required before interpreting every term as a nonnegative divergence or an algorithmic descent guarantee.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Distinct left, middle, and right vectors with a nonconstant supplied gradient give nonzero pairing and divergence differences while retaining exact equality.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep104_mirrorDescent_threePoint_identity for arbitrary finite-dimensional potential and gradient data.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep104_mirrorDescent_threePoint_identity:
theorem fep104_mirrorDescent_threePoint_identity
    (potential : (Fin d → ℝ) → ℝ)
    (gradient : (Fin d → ℝ) → Fin d → ℝ)
    (left middle right : Fin d → ℝ) :
    bregmanDivergence potential gradient left right -
        bregmanDivergence potential gradient left middle -
        bregmanDivergence potential gradient middle right =
      coordinatePairing
        (fun coordinate ↦
          gradient middle coordinate - gradient right coordinate)
        (fun coordinate ↦ left coordinate - middle coordinate)

rows.statement_review: For arbitrary supplied potential and vector field, expanding the defined Bregman expression gives the exact three-point pairing identity. No derivative, convexity, optimizer or descent is asserted.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: The name gradient is data only unless a derivative witness is supplied. Negative Bregman values are permitted for concave potential or inconsistent vector field. Distinct points/nonconstant gradient do not guarantee a nonzero pairing in multiple dimensions, so nonvacuity should give a concrete instance.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Fin1 potential x↦x0^2/2, gradient x↦x0; left2,middle1,right0 gives divergences2,1/2,1/2 and pairing1.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Take concave potential-x0^2/2 with its true gradient-x0: divergence is negative for unequal points although the identity still holds. Orthogonal gradient/point differences can also give zero pairing despite distinct vectors.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 024 is native extended KL regularization. The104 bridge deliberately pairs it without identifying Bregman with KL or deriving a mirror-descent algorithm.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Supplied potential and gradient data satisfy the exact Bregman three-point identity.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Moves from scalar KL regularization to arbitrary finite coordinate potentials, gradient fields, and three comparison points.

rows.title: Bregman Pythagorean Law for an Affine Information Projection

maturity_record.invariant: An affine projection certificate yields exact Bregman Pythagorean splitting, and a nonnegative residual divergence makes the certified projection a minimizer over the maintained affine set.
maturity_record.assumption_review: AffineBregmanProjection explicitly supplies projection membership and gradient-difference orthogonality for every candidate. Minimization separately assumes residual Bregman nonnegativity. Existence, uniqueness, convexity, and differentiability of the projection are not derived.
maturity_record.non_vacuity: Candidates distinct from the projection can have a positive residual term, producing a strict objective gap; zero residual gives the exact equality boundary without proving uniqueness.
maturity_record.acceptance_probe: native Lean compile of fep105_affineProjection_bregmanPythagorean and fep105_affineProjection_minimizes with orthogonality and residual nonnegativity explicit.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep105_affineProjection_bregmanPythagore:
theorem fep105_affineProjection_bregmanPythagorean
    (potential : (Fin d → ℝ) → ℝ)
    (gradient : (Fin d → ℝ) → Fin d → ℝ)
    (affineSet : Set (Fin d → ℝ))
    (base projection candidate : Fin d → ℝ)
    (hProjection : AffineBregmanProjection potential gradient affineSet
      base projection)
    (hCandidate : candidate ∈ affineSet) :
    bregmanDivergence potential gradient candidate base =
      bregmanDivergence potential gradient candidate projection +
        bregmanDivergence potential gradient projection base
qualified_declaration_statements.fep105_affineProjection_minimizes:
theorem fep105_affineProjection_minimizes
    (potential : (Fin d → ℝ) → ℝ)
    (gradient : (Fin d → ℝ) → Fin d → ℝ)
    (affineSet : Set (Fin d → ℝ))
    (base projection candidate : Fin d → ℝ)
    (hProjection : AffineBregmanProjection potential gradient affineSet
      base projection)
    (hCandidate : candidate ∈ affineSet)
    (hNonnegative :
      0 ≤ bregmanDivergence potential gradient candidate projection) :
    bregmanDivergence potential gradient projection base ≤
      bregmanDivergence potential gradient candidate base

rows.statement_review: Projection membership plus supplied orthogonality for every candidate in the named set yields exact splitting. Residual nonnegativity gives a pointwise comparison; a minimizer statement over the whole set needs that premise for every candidate.
rows.assumptions_and_scope: AffineBregmanProjection does not require IsAffine/convexity or derivative/convex potential data; affineSet is merely a Set. The theorem is valid more generally because it assumes full setwise orthogonality. It neither constructs a projection nor proves existence/uniqueness. Hellinger nonnegativity in the relation does not supply this residual Bregman nonnegativity.
rows.positive_witness_specification_unexecute: Quadratic Euclidean potential with true gradient in Fin2, set{x:x1=0}, base(0,1),projection(0,0),candidate(2,0): exact squared-distance splitting with positive residual.
rows.adverse_witness_specification_unexecuted: Without orthogonality the equality need not hold; concave potential can give negative residual so comparison reverses. Finite nonaffine sets can still satisfy the supplied orthogonality certificate, demonstrating no affineness is encoded.
rows.nearest_topic_distinction: 044 squared Hellinger is a separate nonnegative object, not established as this Bregman divergence. Retain conditional_proxy for supplied projection/orthogonality/nonnegative residual.

novelty_record.new_invariant: Affine gradient orthogonality yields Bregman Pythagorean splitting and conditional minimization.
novelty_record.carrier_delta: Adds an affine-set projection certificate and separates exact orthogonality from residual-divergence nonnegativity.

touching_relations.rationale: The affine Bregman projection satisfies its exact Pythagorean identity, while fep-044 records nonnegativity for the concrete Bernoulli Hellinger case.

maturity_record.assumption_review: CategoricalFisherCarrier supplies full support and the exact bridge from the existing ScoreModel lowering map to categorical coordinates. The result is an instantaneous finite-simplex vector-field identity, not positivity preservation or convergence of a time-integrated replicator flow.

qualified_declaration_statements.fep106_replicator_naturalGradient_equiva:
theorem fep106_replicator_naturalGradient_equivalence
    (carrier : CategoricalFisherCarrier d) (fitness : Fin d → ℝ) :
    IsNaturalGradient carrier.model
      (fun coordinate ↦ fitness coordinate - meanFitness carrier.law fitness)
      (replicatorVector carrier.law fitness)
qualified_declaration_statements.fep106_replicator_massConservation:
theorem fep106_replicator_massConservation
    (law : FiniteLaw (Fin d)) (fitness : Fin d → ℝ) :
    ∑ coordinate, replicatorVector law fitness coordinate = 0
qualified_declaration_statements.fep106_twoCategorical_nonzero_replicator:
theorem fep106_twoCategorical_nonzero_replicator_witness :
    twoCategoricalFitness 0 ≠ twoCategoricalFitness 1 ∧
      replicatorVector twoCategoricalLaw twoCategoricalFitness ≠ 0 ∧
      IsNaturalGradient twoCategoricalFisherCarrier.model
        (fun coordinate ↦
          twoCategoricalFitness coordinate -
            meanFitness twoCategoricalLaw twoCategoricalFitness)
        (replicatorVector twoCategoricalLaw twoCategoricalFitness)
